newsitem.title: FRANCE: RUGBY UNION-FRANCE RESIST BRAVE WELSH EFFORT.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-FRANCE RESIST BRAVE WELSH EFFORT.

text.p: A depleted but determined French side shrugged off a brave challenge from Wales to score a 27-22 win at Parc des Princes on Saturday and remain hard on England's heels in the Five Nations race.

France, with six enforced changes from the side who beat Ireland 32-15 in their opening match last month, scored four tries to the visitors' three to set up a title showdown at Twickenham in a fortnight.

Without Emile Ntamack, Philippe Benetton, Thomas Castaignede, Alain Penaud and Fabien Galthie, the French looked clumsy at times but did just enough to prevent Wales collecting their first win in Paris since 1975.
Wales, relying on a powerful back row and brilliant playmaking by flyhalf Arwel Thomas, never gave up despite conceding a try as early as the third minute.
A powerful run by lock Olivier Merle, plus a conversion from Richard Dourthe gave the French an immediate 7-0 cushion but any thoughts of an easy home win were swiftly banished.
Wales fought back and after a couple of scrums near the French try line, winger Gareth Thomas perforated a porous French defence for a 16th minute try which Neil Jenkins converted.
A Jenkins penalty saw the visitors move in front four minutes later as Dourthe left the pitch with a dislocated shoulder which will keep him out of action for six weeks.
But France's speed and ability to run the ball were then illustrated with two tries in the last five minutes of the first half, both sparked by the impressive Christophe Lamaison.
Winger Laurent Leflamand followed up a kick by the Brive fly-half and dived over for a try in the 35th minute and three minutes later, Lamaison set up David Venditti to give France five more points.
After Lamaison failed to convert both tries, Dourthe's replacement David Aucagne took over the goalkicking duties and put over a penalty just before the teams changed sides with France leading 20-10.
Feeling a historic upset was possible, Wales gave their all and in the 56th minute, veteran winger Ieuan Evans escaped to put centre Alan Bateman over for a try converted by Jenkins.

France led by a mere 20-17 at that point and had every reason to worry about the near future when two Welsh players, surprised by a vicious bounce, failed to gather the ball dangerously close to their line in the 65th minute.
Leflamand used the blunder to score his second try and Aucagne converted it to put France 27-17 up.

There was still time for Welsh number eight Scott Quinnell to set up scrum-half Robert Howley for a try which raised Welsh hopes again, but the tricky conversion was missed by Jenkins and France held on.
"Every time France had an opportunity, they scored a try," said Wales hooker and captain Jonathan Humphreys. "That's typical of the French game."
France will now travel to Twickenham to face England on March 1 dreaming not only of victory in the tournament but also of a possible grand slam.
"It was a bit of a crazy match, sometimes brilliant and sometimes dull," said Merle. "That win will do our confidence a lot of good before going to England."
Teams

France: 15-Jean-Luc Sadourny; 14-Laurent Leflamand, 13-Richard Dourthe (17-David Aucagne, 21st), 12-Stephane Glas, 11-David Venditti; 10-Christophe Lamaison, 9-Philippe Carbonneau; 8-Fabien Pelous, 7-Richard Castel, 6-Abdel Benazzi (captain), 5-Hugues Miorin (19-Olivier Magne, 57th), 4-Olivier Merle, 3-Jean-Louis Jordana, 2-Marc Dal Maso, 1-Christian Califano

Wales: 15-Neil Jenkins; 14-Ieuan Evans (16-Jonathan Davies, 56th), 13-Alan Bateman, 12-Scott Gibbs, 11-Gareth Thomas; 10-Arwel Thomas, 9-Rob Howley; 8-Scott Quinnell, 7-Colin Charvis, 6-Steve Williams, 5-Mark Rowley, 4-Gareth Llewellyn, 3-David Young, 2-Jonathan Humphreys (captain), 1-Christian Loader.
